name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

highLevelGoals: To successfully register and provide necessary company and payment information to become a recognized supplier.
To submit product proposals with all required details for evaluation by La Reine Marlene.
To receive and act upon feedback regarding product proposals, including making revisions and resubmitting within deadlines.
To be paid for products that have been successfully ordered and delivered.
To review and make timely decisions on product proposals submitted by suppliers, ensuring business relevance and quality.
To provide clear and actionable feedback to suppliers regarding the acceptance, rejection, or need for revisions of their proposals.
To prevent delays in the evaluation process by receiving reminders and adhering to evaluation deadlines.
To ensure that all incoming products match order specifications and are free from damage or discrepancies.
To effectively document and report any problems found with delivered products to prevent them from entering the store.
To efficiently assign and direct products to appropriate store locations for display and sale.
To place products in their designated store locations promptly after reception.
To print and apply correct retail prices to products for customer purchase.
To process the outcomes of product deliveries, ensuring orders are completed or updated appropriately.
To facilitate timely payment to suppliers for successfully delivered and accepted products.
To receive notifications about critical inventory thresholds and manage reordering processes to prevent stockouts.
To configure and manage rules for automatic reordering and replenishment of products.
To browse the product catalogue, select items, and complete purchases conveniently through online channels.
To make payments for purchases using a variety of trusted and convenient methods.
To monitor the real-time status of their online orders and receive timely updates on shipment progress.
To submit questions, requests, or complaints and receive prompt and effective assistance.
To receive delivery assignments and accurately update the status of shipments to ensure timely product delivery.
To respond to customer support tickets within established timeframes and resolve customer issues effectively.
To ensure that customer support metrics are updated to reflect service efficiency and agent performance.
To access and analyze comprehensive data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support for informed strategic decision-making.
To identify areas for improvement and optimize business processes based on collected performance data.

The system should allow the customer to download the invoice for a specific past order.
The system should allow the customer to retrieve real-time status updates, carrier details, and tracking numbers for a specific order.
The system should allow the customer to opt-in to receive delivery tracking notifications via email or mobile.
The system should allow the customer to submit a new support ticket with a subject and description for questions or complaints.
The system should allow the customer to retrieve a list of all their submitted support tickets.
The system should allow the customer to view the details and message history of a specific support ticket.
The system should allow the customer to add a new message or reply to an existing support ticket.
The customer requests the system to provide a list of all supported payment methods (e.g., credit card, PayPal, bank transfer) to choose from for their purchase.
The customer sends a request to the system to associate a chosen payment method (e.g., 'Credit Card') with their current order during the checkout process.
The customer securely sends their encrypted credit card number, expiration date, and CVV to the system for processing a payment.
The customer requests the system to initiate a PayPal transaction, leading to a redirection to the PayPal gateway or presentation of an embedded PayPal interface.
The customer sends a confirmation to the system to finalize the payment process for a specific transaction after reviewing the details.
The system provides the customer with the current status (e.g., successful, pending, failed) of their payment attempt after submission.
The system shall allow the customer to retrieve a paginated list of all their placed orders, including basic order identifiers and current high-level status.
The system shall allow the customer to retrieve comprehensive details for a specific order using its unique order identifier, including items purchased, total cost, and current overall status.
The system shall allow the customer to retrieve the current delivery status (e.g., 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'In Transit', 'Delivered') and estimated delivery date for a specific order.
The system shall allow the customer to retrieve a chronological list of all tracking events (e.g., 'Package picked up', 'Arrived at sorting facility', 'Out for delivery') for a specific order.
The system shall allow the customer to subscribe to real-time notifications (e.g., email, SMS, push notification) for status changes of a specific order.
The system shall allow the customer to unsubscribe from real-time notifications for status changes of a specific order.
The customer can create a new support ticket by providing a subject, detailed description, and optionally, attaching relevant files.
The customer can retrieve a paginated list of all support tickets they have previously submitted, including their current status and creation date.
The customer can retrieve the full details and chronological conversation history of a specific support ticket using its unique identifier.
The customer can post a new message or reply to an ongoing conversation within an existing support ticket.
The customer can update the status of an open support ticket to 'resolved' once their issue has been satisfactorily addressed.
The customer can submit a numerical rating (e.g., 1-5 stars) and an optional text comment for a completed support ticket interaction.
The Shipping Provider needs to query the system to get a list of all delivery assignments that are pending acceptance.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to accept a particular delivery assignment, changing its status from 'pending' to 'accepted'.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to reject a particular delivery assignment, providing a reason for rejection.
The Shipping Provider needs to query the system to get detailed information (e.g., recipient address, package contents, special instructions) for an accepted delivery assignment.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to change the status of a specific shipment to 'Picked Up' once the package has been collected.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to change the status of a specific shipment to 'In Transit' once it begins its journey.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to change the status of a specific shipment to 'Delivered' upon successful completion of the delivery.
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to upload a digital signature or photo as proof of delivery for a specific shipment.

The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to change the status of a specific shipment to 'Delivery Attempted' and provide a reason (e.g., 'recipient not available', 'address inaccessible').
The Shipping Provider needs to send a request to the system to update the current geographical coordinates or a descriptive location for a specific shipment.
The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to fetch a list of all support tickets currently assigned to their agent ID, regardless of status (e.g., 'New', 'In Progress', 'Pending Customer Response').
The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to fetch all details, including customer information, issue description, and communication history, for a specific support ticket ID.

The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to change the status of a newly assigned support ticket from 'New' to 'In Progress', indicating they have started working on it and initiating the 24-hour response timeframe.
The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to post a new text-based response or comment to a specific support ticket, which will be visible to the customer.
The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to change the status of a support ticket to 'Pending Customer Response' after providing an initial reply and awaiting further input from the customer.

The Customer-Service Agent can call an API to change the status of a support ticket to 'Resolved' once the customer's issue has been fully addressed and confirmed, or after a predefined period if no further customer response is received.

The Customer-Service Agent needs to claim an unassigned support ticket, thereby updating the ticket's owner and initiating the tracking of the agent's handling time for that ticket. This action contributes to individual workload and response time metrics.

The Customer-Service Agent needs to post a new message or internal note to an active support ticket, which updates the ticket's communication log and contributes to response time and interaction count metrics.

The Customer-Service Agent needs to change the status of a completed support ticket to 'Resolved', which marks the end of the agent's handling time and contributes to their individual ticket resolution rate.

The Customer-Service Agent needs to reassign an open support ticket to a different agent or department, which updates the ticket's ownership and contributes to transfer metrics and overall service flow analysis.

The system shall allow Company Management to retrieve a list of all defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their current aggregated values.
The system shall allow Company Management to query performance data for specific KPIs, filtered by a defined time range and relevant business dimensions (e.g., department, product line, region).

high_level_goal.name: Propose Products for Sale
high_level_goal.description: To submit product proposals with all required details for evaluation by La Reine Marlene.

actor.name: Supplier
actor.description: Registers, submits product proposals, and receives notifications and payments.

evaluation.rationale:
The current set of Low-Level Goals (LLGs) provides a comprehensive and logically structured decomposition of the High-Level Goal 'Propose Products for Sale'. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to the supplier's interaction with the proposal lifecycle, from registration (prerequisite) to submission, revision, and post-submission tracking (status, notifications, payments). 
2. **Consistency**: The goals align with the project description. For instance, llg_011 and llg_013 correctly handle the 'Revisions Requested' workflow described in the text. llg_016 addresses the 'Confirm Automatic Product Reorder' capability, which is explicitly mentioned in the project description as a supplier action ('who has two working days to confirm it'). Although this occurs after the initial proposal is accepted, it is a distinct functional intention tied to the supplier's role in the product supply chain and is not duplicated by other LLGs. 
3. **No Duplicates/Contradictions**: There are no clear duplicates. llg_005 (Update Draft) and llg_011 (Revise Submitted) are distinct based on the proposal's status (draft vs. returned for revision). llg_009 (Submit) and llg_013 (Resubmit) are distinct actions in the workflow. 
4. **Missing Capabilities**: The core capabilities for proposing products (registration, authentication, category selection, detail entry, pricing, image upload, submission, revision handling, and status tracking) are all covered. The inclusion of payment status (llg_015) and notification details (llg_014) supports the 'receives notifications and payments' aspect of the actor description and the HLG context. 

Therefore, the existing LLGs are supported and should be kept.

high_level_goal.name: Respond to Proposal Feedback
high_level_goal.description: To receive and act upon feedback regarding product proposals, including making revisions and resubmitting within deadlines.

actor.name: Supplier
actor.description: Registers, submits product proposals, and receives notifications and payments.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' for the Supplier actor. 

1. **llg_001 (RetrievePendingFeedbackProposals)**: Essential for identifying which proposals require action. Supported by the requirement that suppliers are notified and must act within deadlines.
2. **llg_002 (ViewSpecificProposalFeedback)**: Essential for understanding the 'revisions requested' outcome, which requires the administration to explain revisions in a comment. The supplier needs to view these to act upon them.
3. **llg_003 (UpdateProposalContent)**: Directly supports the requirement to 'modify the proposal'.
4. **llg_004 (UploadRevisedProposalDocuments)**: The project description states proposals include 'photos, description'. Modifying a proposal may involve updating these assets. This is a valid fine-grained capability supporting the revision process.
5. **llg_005 (ResubmitRevisedProposal)**: Explicitly required ('resubmit it').
6. **llg_006 (CheckRevisedProposalStatus)**: While the primary flow ends with resubmission, checking status is a standard and reasonable capability for a supplier to verify if their resubmission has been received or is under review, especially given the 5-day window and subsequent automatic rejection if not handled. It is not unrelated or contradictory.

No LLGs are duplicated, contradictory, or unrelated. No essential capabilities are missing for the specific scope of 'Responding to Feedback' (i.e., the act of revising and resubmitting). The handling of the deadline expiration (automatic removal) is a system/admin action, not a supplier action, so it does not require an LLG here.

evaluation.rationale:

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' for the Administration Department. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to the evaluation process described in the project documentation (retrieving proposals, viewing details, making decisions, requesting revisions, and handling notifications/reminders).
2. **Consistency**: 
   - `llg_001` and `llg_006` are distinct: one is a general retrieval of all proposals, the other is a filtered view for actionable items/deadlines. This is a valid distinction for efficient workflow management.
   - `llg_003` (Update status) and `llg_005` (Request revisions) are distinct: `llg_005` specifically covers the 'revisions requested' outcome which requires comments and triggers a specific supplier workflow (5-day deadline), whereas `llg_003` covers the general state change (including 'Accepted' or 'Rejected'). While there is overlap in the 'Rejected' case, `llg_005` is specific to the revision workflow mandated by the requirements. Keeping both is conservative and safe.
   - `llg_004` (Submit feedback) and `llg_005` (Request revisions): `llg_005` explicitly includes 'providing detailed reasons', which covers the comment aspect for that specific action. `llg_004` is a general capability that might apply to other contexts or be a prerequisite, but it is not clearly duplicated by `llg_005` in a way that makes it misleading. It is a fine-grained API-oriented goal, which is acceptable.
   - `llg_007` (New proposal notifications) and `llg_008` (Reminders for pending proposals) are distinct based on the documentation: one triggers on submission, the other is a periodic reminder (every 48 hours) for pending items.

high_level_goal.name: Accurately Verify Delivered Goods
high_level_goal.description: To ensure that all incoming products match order specifications and are free from damage or discrepancies.

actor.name: Goods-Receiving Staff
actor.description: Verifies delivered products, reports issues, and assigns store locations.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Accurately Verify Delivered Goods' for the 'Goods-Receiving Staff' actor. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to the verification process described in the project documentation (checking products, reporting problems, confirming items, assigning locations). 
2. **Consistency**: 
   - `llg_001` (Retrieve details) is necessary to know what to expect.
   - `llg_002` (Scan/Identify) is the mechanism to link physical goods to system records.
   - `llg_003` (Record Quantity) addresses the 'available quantity' and 'match order specifications' aspect.
   - `llg_004` (Report Damaged) and `llg_005` (Report Discrepancy) cover the 'If a problem is detected' branch where the operator reports issues via comments/details.
   - `llg_006` (Mark Verified) covers the 'If no problem is found' branch.
   - `llg_007` (Assign Location) covers the specific requirement that 'the system proposes a list of possible store locations' and the operator selects one. Note: While the documentation says the product is then passed to staff for placement, the *assignment* of the location is part of the receiving/verification workflow before handover.
   - `llg_008` (Finalize) covers the completion of the receipt process for the order.

3. **No Duplicates/Contradictions**: There are no clear duplicates. `llg_004` and `llg_005` are distinct (damage vs. quantity/type mismatch). `llg_006` is the positive confirmation, distinct from the negative reports. 

4. **Missing Capabilities**: The documentation mentions that if a problem is detected, the product is 'not admitted into the store'. This is implicitly handled by the reporting actions (llg_004/005) which prevent the 'MarkItemAsVerified' (llg_006) or 'AssignStoreDisplayLocation' (llg_007) from being validly executed for that item. No explicit 'RejectItem' LLG is strictly necessary if the state change is implied by the report, but the current set covers the *verification* aspect well. The HLG is about *verifying*, not necessarily the downstream logistics of rejection, though the report is the verification outcome. The set is sufficient for the HLG scope.

Therefore, the LLGs are supported and accurate.

branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process a supplier undergoes to join the system, from initial account creation and providing essential business and payment information, through submitting it for administrative review, to receiving final approval or rejection. This entire sequence of operations is aimed at successfully bringing a new supplier into the system and establishing a business relationship, which is encapsulated by the term 'onboarding'.

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Suppliers to Manage Product Proposals and Approved Products
branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a supplier's interaction with the system, starting from registration and authentication, moving through the creation, detailed specification, submission, and revision of product proposals, and finally extending to the management of approved products, including viewing notifications, tracking payments, and responding to reorder requests. All these operations are essential for a supplier to effectively propose new products and manage their existing approved products within the system.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View Status of Own Product Proposals
Add Revision Response Comments to Proposal

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Revise and Resubmit Product Proposals Based on Feedback
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for a supplier to identify product proposals requiring attention, understand the feedback received, make necessary modifications and updates, formally resubmit the revised proposals, and monitor their subsequent review status. They form a coherent set of operations aimed at successfully addressing feedback and advancing a proposal through the evaluation process.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Supplier Payouts for Completed Orders
branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of functionalities a Supplier requires to effectively manage the reception of automatic payments from the system. This includes configuring payment details, acknowledging payment triggers, monitoring the status of individual and aggregated payments, and reviewing a historical record of all received payouts for completed orders.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Update registered bank account details for receiving payments
Retrieve list of completed orders that triggered automatic payment
Check automatic payment status for a specific completed order
View history of all automatic payments received

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of functionalities required by the Administration Department to oversee the entire lifecycle of product proposals. This includes capabilities for discovery (retrieving lists, notifications), detailed examination (viewing details, attachments), active review and decision-making (changing status, adding feedback, requesting revisions), and proactive monitoring (filtered lists, reminders). All these actions are integral to the effective management and processing of product proposals from submission to final resolution.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View detailed information of a specific product proposal
Update the status of a product proposal
Submit feedback or comments on a product proposal
Request revisions for a product proposal
Retrieve a list of proposals requiring attention or nearing deadlines
Retrieve notifications for new product proposals
Retrieve reminders for pending product proposals

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Supplier Proposal Evaluation and Response
branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for the Administration Department to evaluate supplier proposals by reviewing details, attachments, pricing, and availability; make a decision (accept, reject, or request revision); provide necessary feedback; and communicate the final outcome to the supplier, with system support for timely processing. All these operations are integral steps in effectively handling and responding to incoming supplier proposals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Retrieve specific proposal details for evaluation
Access proposal attachments for detailed review
Compare proposed pricing with internal guidelines
Verify proposed product availability and lead times
Provide mandatory textual explanation for requested revisions
Add general textual feedback message to a proposal
Trigger email notification to supplier for proposal outcome

branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of activities and system support required for the Administration Department to effectively manage and conduct the entire proposal evaluation process. This includes monitoring deadlines, accessing proposal details, requesting revisions, and making final acceptance or rejection decisions.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Receive automated reminder for an upcoming proposal evaluation deadline
Retrieve a list of all proposals currently assigned for evaluation, including their respective deadlines
Retrieve detailed information for a specific proposal to initiate evaluation
Request a revision for a specific proposal from the submitter

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Receipt and Verification of Incoming Goods
branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive process undertaken by Goods-Receiving Staff to handle incoming inventory. They encompass retrieving purchase order details, identifying received items, recording quantities, reporting discrepancies or damage, verifying item quality, assigning storage locations, and ultimately finalizing the goods receipt process. All these operations are essential steps to ensure that ordered goods are correctly received, accounted for, and prepared for subsequent inventory management or display.

branch_009.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete set of actions a Goods-Receiving Staff member performs to identify, report, detail, submit, and monitor discrepancies found during the goods receiving process. They cover the creation, modification, submission, and retrieval of product discrepancy reports, indicating a comprehensive management process.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Add Comment to Product Discrepancy Report

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for goods-receiving staff, encompassing product identification, quantity verification, discrepancy handling, location assignment, labeling, and final placement confirmation. These operations are all integral parts of the overall process of admitting new products into inventory and preparing them for storage or sale.

branch_011.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Product Placement and Labeling on the Sales Floor
branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the end-to-end process for store staff to take products that have been received and verified, determine their final display locations, physically place them on the sales floor, update the inventory system to reflect their placement, and finally generate and print the necessary price labels for these newly placed products. They represent a complete workflow for stocking and preparing products for sale.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Request Price Label Generation for Placed Products

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Product Price Label Generation and Printing
branch_012.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe a complete workflow for identifying products that require new price labels (due to absence or price changes), retrieving necessary product information, generating the formatted labels, and finally sending them to a printer for physical output. All these operations are sequential steps aimed at ensuring accurate and up-to-date physical price labels are available for products in the store.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Retrieve products requiring price label updates
Fetch current retail price and product details
Send generated price labels to a designated printer

branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of activities performed by the Order Department related to procuring products. This includes initiating orders (both automatically based on inventory levels and manually), sending these orders to suppliers, managing the reception of products, updating order statuses (e.g., 'fulfilled', 'delivery problem'), handling issues during admission, triggering payments, and querying order status. All these operations are integral parts of overseeing the entire lifecycle of product orders from creation to their successful fulfillment and payment.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Trigger Supplier Payment for Fulfilled Order
Update Order Status to Delivery Problem
Access Automatic Critical Inventory Level Notifications

branch_014.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable the Order Department to efficiently manage the end-to-end Procure-to-Pay process.
branch_014.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the functionalities required by the Order Department to manage the entire procurement lifecycle. This includes identifying inventory needs and creating purchase orders (llg_007, llg_008, llg_009, llg_010), tracking the status of these orders based on goods reception (llg_011, llg_012, llg_013), and finally, processing supplier invoices against accepted deliveries and purchase orders to facilitate payment (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003, llg_004, llg_005, llg_006). These operations are interdependent and form the complete 'Procure-to-Pay' process, ensuring efficient and accurate acquisition of goods and services and timely supplier payments.

branch_015.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Procurement and Replenishment of Inventory
branch_015.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of acquiring goods to replenish inventory. They cover identifying the need for stock (notifications, queries), configuring reorder processes (rules), creating and managing purchase orders (manual, automated, approval, submission, tracking), handling goods receipt, and initiating payment. All these operations are interdependent steps within a comprehensive procurement process aimed at maintaining optimal inventory levels.

branch_016.rationale: All low-level goals describe various operations an Administrator performs to define, modify, enable, disable, remove, and view the configuration of rules governing automatic product replenishment. These operations collectively constitute the comprehensive management of such rules within the system.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Set Rule Condition: Minimum Stock Level

branch_017.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Customer's End-to-End Online Shopping Experience
branch_017.rationale: These low-level goals collectively define the complete set of functionalities required for a customer to interact with an online retail system. They encompass the entire customer journey, from account creation and management, through product browsing, selection, and purchasing, to post-purchase activities like order tracking and customer support. All operations are essential components of a comprehensive e-commerce platform from the customer's perspective.

branch_018.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Process Customer Payment for an Order
branch_018.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for a customer to make a payment for an order. This includes selecting a payment method, providing the necessary details for the chosen method, initiating the transaction, confirming the payment, and receiving feedback on its status. All these operations are integral steps in successfully processing a customer's payment.

branch_019.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Customer Order Tracking and Notification Management
branch_019.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide customers with comprehensive capabilities to monitor the status and details of their placed orders, from a high-level overview to specific tracking events, and to manage how they receive real-time updates about these orders. They cover both information retrieval and notification subscription/unsubscription for order status changes.

branch_020.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a customer's interaction with support tickets, from creation and tracking to communication, resolution, and feedback. They all contribute to empowering the customer to effectively manage their support requests and interactions.

branch_021.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Delivery Operations and Shipment Lifecycle
branch_021.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete set of actions a Shipping Provider needs to perform to handle delivery assignments and manage shipments throughout their lifecycle. This includes querying and accepting/rejecting assignments, retrieving detailed information, updating shipment statuses at various stages (picked up, in transit, delivered, attempted delivery), providing proof of delivery, and updating location information. All these operations are essential for the Shipping Provider to effectively execute and monitor the delivery process from start to finish.

branch_022.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Customer-Service Agents to Process Assigned Support Tickets
branch_022.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential functionalities required by a Customer-Service Agent to effectively manage the lifecycle of support tickets assigned to them. This includes viewing tickets, accessing their details, updating their status through various stages (from 'New' to 'In Progress', 'Pending Customer Response', and 'Resolved'), and communicating with customers by posting responses. All operations are centered around the agent's ability to process and resolve customer issues represented by support tickets.

branch_023.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions a Customer-Service Agent performs to manage the lifecycle of a support ticket, from taking ownership and communicating with customers to resolving or reassigning the ticket, all while contributing to key performance metrics related to service efficiency and agent performance.

branch_024.rationale: The low-level goals collectively provide Company Management with diverse capabilities to retrieve, filter, report on, and analyze data across critical business domains including sales, orders, inventory, and customer support. These functionalities are all geared towards gaining comprehensive visibility into the company's operational status, evaluating its performance, identifying trends, and supporting informed strategic and operational decision-making.

branch_025.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Comprehensive Business Performance Monitoring and Analysis for Company Management

replacement_request.rationale: The original HLG name 'Establish Business Relationship' is too broad and abstract. The requirements specifically detail a registration process where the supplier provides credentials, company information (VAT, address), and payment details (IBAN). The evaluator suggests renaming to 'Facilitate Supplier Onboarding' or 'Complete Supplier Registration' to accurately reflect this setup phase. I will use 'Complete Supplier Registration' as it is more precise regarding the action of providing the necessary data to become a recognized supplier. The focus is strictly on the initial registration and setup, excluding subsequent proposal submission or order management activities.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time. After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected. If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified. Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier. Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location. During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store. At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier. The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products. In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process. Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks. Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed. Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application. The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated. When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed. Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Propose Products for Sale' is supported by the project description, which details the supplier's ability to submit proposals with specific attributes (category, price, availability, etc.). However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Suppliers to Manage Product Proposals and Approved Products' suggests a broader scope that includes managing approved products. Looking at the other existing High-Level Goals for the Supplier actor, we see 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' (covering revisions) and 'Receive Payment for Accepted Orders' (covering the outcome of approved products). The original goal 'Propose Products for Sale' specifically targets the initial submission phase. The reconstruction seems to conflate the submission phase with the management of the resulting approved products (which is largely covered by payment and potentially other implicit goals, though 'Manage Approved Products' isn't explicitly a separate HLG, the payment goal covers the financial aspect). However, the core intention of the original goal is to *submit* the proposal. The reconstruction is broader. Is the original goal too narrow? The project description says suppliers 'submit proposals'. It doesn't explicitly describe a 'manage approved products' workflow for the supplier other than receiving payment and notifications. The 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' goal covers the revision cycle. The 'Receive Payment' goal covers the post-approval financial aspect. The original goal 'Propose Products for Sale' accurately captures the primary action of creating and submitting the initial proposal. The reconstruction 'Manage Product Proposals and Approved Products' is vague regarding 'Approved Products' since the supplier's interaction with approved products is primarily passive (receiving payment/notifications) or handled by the 'Respond to Feedback' goal if revisions are needed. The original goal is a distinct, supported functional intention: the act of proposing. It is not generic. It is not incorrectly scoped. It is distinct from 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' (which is about reacting to admin decisions) and 'Receive Payment' (which is about the financial outcome). Therefore, the original goal is a valid, specific, and supported intention. The reconstruction is less precise because 'Manage Approved Products' is not a clearly defined active workflow for the supplier in the text, whereas 'Propose Products' is. Keeping the original goal maintains clarity and alignment with the specific submission workflow described. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are explicitly owned by sibling High-Level Goals (HLGs), violating the separation of concerns. Specifically: 
1. 'Register Supplier Account' (llg_001) and 'Authenticate Supplier Session' (llg_002) belong to the sibling HLG 'Establish Business Relationship'. 
2. 'Revise Submitted Product Proposal' (llg_011), 'Add Revision Response Comments to Proposal' (llg_012), and 'Resubmit Revised Product Proposal' (llg_013) belong to the sibling HLG 'Respond to Proposal Feedback'. 
3. 'View Supplier Payment Status' (llg_015) belongs to the sibling HLG 'Receive Payment for Accepted Orders'. 
4. 'Confirm Automatic Product Reorder' (llg_016) is part of the order management/replenishment process, typically associated with 'Manage Order Fulfillment' or 'Automate Replenishment Processes', and is not a core part of the initial 'Propose Products for Sale' lifecycle which ends upon submission/acceptance. 

The parent HLG 'Propose Products for Sale' focuses on the creation and submission of new proposals. The current LLGs mix in registration, feedback handling, payment tracking, and reorder confirmation, which are distinct business processes. Therefore, the decomposition is flawed due to duplication of sibling responsibilities.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback: Remove LLGs that belong to sibling HLGs: 'Register Supplier Account' (llg_001), 'Authenticate Supplier Session' (llg_002), 'Revise Submitted Product Proposal' (llg_011), 'Add Revision Response Comments to Proposal' (llg_012), 'Resubmit Revised Product Proposal' (llg_013), 'View Supplier Payment Status' (llg_015), and 'Confirm Automatic Product Reorder' (llg_016). Focus the LLGs strictly on the creation, detailing, and submission of new product proposals, including retrieving categories, creating drafts, adding details (price, availability, photos, description, delivery time), and submitting for review. Viewing status of *own* proposals (llg_010) and retrieving notification details (llg_014) may be retained if they are considered part of the proposal lifecycle management, but ensure they do not overlap with 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' (Admin side) or 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' (Supplier side action). Given the strict sibling separation, it is safer to keep only the core proposal creation and submission steps.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Respond to Proposal Feedback' is supported by the project description, which details the process where suppliers receive revision requests, modify proposals, add comments, and resubmit within a 5-day deadline. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Revise and Resubmit Product Proposals Based on Feedback' is semantically equivalent but slightly more specific regarding the action (revise/resubmit) rather than the general state (respond). However, the original goal is not generic, narrow, or incorrectly scoped; it accurately captures the supplier's intention to handle the feedback loop. The other existing HLGs for the Supplier ('Establish Business Relationship', 'Propose Products for Sale', 'Receive Payment for Accepted Orders') do not overlap with this specific feedback handling process. Therefore, the original goal is valid and should be kept. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the workflow described in the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Respond to Proposal Feedback'. 
1. **RetrievePendingFeedbackProposals** (llg_001) addresses the need to identify proposals requiring attention.
2. **ViewSpecificProposalFeedback** (llg_002) allows the supplier to understand the specific revisions requested.
3. **UpdateProposalContent** (llg_003) and **UploadRevisedProposalDocuments** (llg_004) cover the modification of the proposal data and supporting materials, which aligns with the documentation stating the supplier must 'modify the proposal'.
4. **ResubmitRevisedProposal** (llg_005) covers the formal action of resubmitting within the deadline.
5. **CheckRevisedProposalStatus** (llg_006) allows the supplier to monitor the outcome of the resubmission.

The documentation mentions that the supplier has five working days to modify and resubmit. While the LLGs do not explicitly include a 'Check Deadline' or 'Receive Deadline Notification' goal, the HLG description focuses on 'making revisions and resubmitting within deadlines'. The act of resubmitting (llg_005) inherently implies adherence to the deadline, and the system's automatic rejection upon timeout is a system-side behavior (often handled by background jobs or the evaluation HLG) rather than a distinct supplier action goal. The supplier's primary responsibility is to perform the revision and resubmission. The existing LLGs capture the essential supplier actions required to fulfill the HLG. There are no contradictions with the documentation, and no essential supplier capabilities are missing. The granularity is appropriate for API-mappable goals.

branch_004.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Receive Payment for Accepted Orders' accurately captures the supplier's intention to be compensated for successfully delivered goods. The project description explicitly states that 'the supplier is paid' when an order is completed. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Payouts for Completed Orders' is semantically equivalent but uses more administrative/managerial language ('Manage') which is less appropriate for the Supplier actor, who is the recipient of the payment rather than the manager of the payout process. The original goal is supported, correctly scoped to the Supplier actor, and distinct from the Order Department's goal 'Ensure Supplier Payments' (which focuses on the action of facilitating payment). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the Supplier's perspective on receiving payments. 
1. **Configuration**: llg_001 covers updating bank details, which is essential for receiving payments (distinct from initial registration in 'Establish Business Relationship').
2. **Notification/Acknowledgement**: llg_005 covers acknowledging the completion notification, which triggers the awareness of the payment process.
3. **Monitoring**: llg_002 and llg_003 allow the supplier to check which orders are paid and the specific status of a payment, addressing the need to monitor the status of individual and aggregated payments.
4. **History**: llg_004 provides a historical record of all received payouts.

The parent HLG 'Receive Payment for Accepted Orders' is satisfied by these capabilities. The actual execution of the payment (transferring funds) is the responsibility of the 'Order Department' (sibling HLG 'Ensure Supplier Payments'), so it is correctly excluded from the Supplier's LLGs. There are no missing essential capabilities for the Supplier actor, and no LLGs are contradicted by the documentation.

branch_005.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' is supported by the project description, which states that the administration department evaluates proposals and chooses among accepted, revisions requested, or rejected. However, looking at the other current High-Level Goals for the same actor, there is significant semantic overlap. Specifically, 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' covers the decision-making aspect (accept/reject/revise) and the feedback provision, while 'Ensure Timely Proposal Processing' covers the monitoring and deadline aspects. The original goal 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' is a broad umbrella that encompasses the core action of evaluation. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, it is preferable to have distinct, non-overlapping goals. The act of 'evaluating' is the primary functional intention. The other two goals ('Communicate...' and 'Ensure Timely...') are arguably sub-goals or specific aspects of the evaluation process (communication of the result and adherence to time constraints). Keeping 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' as the primary goal is valid, but the presence of 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' creates a split in the intention: one focuses on the decision/feedback, the other on the evaluation process. However, 'Evaluate' inherently includes making the decision. 'Communicate' is the mechanism. 'Ensure Timely' is a constraint. The original goal is reasonably scoped and captures the main functional intent of the actor regarding proposals. The other goals are more specific facets. Therefore, the original goal is supported and distinct enough as the primary functional goal for the actor's interaction with proposals. It is not generic or incorrectly scoped. It is the core activity. The other goals are complementary. Thus, it should be kept. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential capabilities required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals'. 

1. **Discovery & Monitoring**: LLG_001 (Retrieve all), LLG_006 (Retrieve filtered/attention), LLG_007 (New proposal notifications), and LLG_008 (Reminders for pending) cover the discovery and proactive monitoring aspects. The documentation states administrators are notified of new proposals and receive reminders every 48 hours for pending ones. These are well-represented.
2. **Examination**: LLG_002 (View detailed information) covers the need to review product details, photos, descriptions, etc., which is necessary for evaluation.
3. **Decision Making**: LLG_003 (Update status) covers the core action of accepting or rejecting. LLG_005 (Request revisions) covers the specific workflow for requesting changes, which includes providing reasons. LLG_004 (Submit feedback/comments) is a general capability that supports the revision request and general communication during review.

The sibling HLG 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' might seem to overlap with LLG_004/005, but the current HLG is about the *evaluation* process itself. The act of updating the status and requesting revisions is part of the evaluation. The communication aspect is the mechanism by which the evaluation result is conveyed. The LLGs correctly focus on the administrative actions (updating status, requesting revisions) rather than just the notification mechanism (which is often a system side-effect or part of the status update). The sibling HLG 'Ensure Timely Proposal Processing' covers the deadline enforcement logic (auto-rejection after 10 days), which is a system rule, not an active user goal for the administrator to *perform* an action, although the administrator needs to be aware of deadlines (covered by LLG_006/008). The auto-rejection is a system behavior, not an LLG for the admin to 'reject' manually in that specific timeout case, but the admin's goal is to evaluate *before* that happens. The current LLGs support this. 

There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

However, looking at the other current High-Level Goals for the same actor, there is significant semantic overlap. Specifically, 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' covers the decision-making aspect (accept/reject/revise) and the feedback provision, while 'Ensure Timely Proposal Processing' covers the monitoring and deadline aspects. The original goal 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' is a broad umbrella that encompasses the core action of evaluation. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, it is preferable to have distinct, non-overlapping goals. The act of 'evaluating' is the primary functional intention. The other two goals ('Communicate...' and 'Ensure Timely...') are arguably sub-goals or specific aspects of the evaluation process (communication of the result and adherence to time constraints). Keeping 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' as the primary goal is valid, but the presence of 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' creates a split in the intention: one focuses on the decision/feedback, the other on the evaluation process. However, 'Evaluate' inherently includes making the decision. 'Communicate' is the mechanism. 'Ensure Timely' is a constraint. The original goal is reasonably scoped and captures the main functional intent of the actor regarding proposals. The other goals are more specific facets. Therefore, the original goal is supported and distinct enough as the primary functional goal for the actor's interaction with proposals. It is not generic or incorrectly scoped. It is the core activity. The other goals are complementary. Thus, it should be kept.

low_level_evaluation.rationale:
The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential capabilities required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals'. 

1. **Discovery & Monitoring**: LLG_001 (Retrieve all), LLG_006 (Retrieve filtered/attention), LLG_007 (New proposal notifications), and LLG_008 (Reminders for pending) cover the discovery and proactive monitoring aspects. The documentation states administrators are notified of new proposals and receive reminders every 48 hours for pending ones. These are well-represented.
2. **Examination**: LLG_002 (View detailed information) covers the need to review product details, photos, descriptions, etc., which is necessary for evaluation.
3. **Decision Making**: LLG_003 (Update status) covers the core action of accepting or rejecting. LLG_005 (Request revisions) covers the specific workflow for requesting changes, which includes providing reasons. LLG_004 (Submit feedback/comments) is a general capability that supports the revision request and general communication during review.

The sibling HLG 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' might seem to overlap with LLG_004/005, but the current HLG is about the *evaluation* process itself. The act of updating the status and requesting revisions is part of the evaluation. The communication aspect is the mechanism by which the evaluation result is conveyed. The LLGs correctly focus on the administrative actions (updating status, requesting revisions) rather than just the notification mechanism (which is often a system side-effect or part of the status update). The sibling HLG 'Ensure Timely Proposal Processing' covers the deadline enforcement logic (auto-rejection after 10 days), which is a system rule, not an active user goal for the administrator to *perform* an action, although the administrator needs to be aware of deadlines (covered by LLG_006/008). The auto-rejection is a system behavior, not an LLG for the admin to 'reject' manually in that specific timeout case, but the admin's goal is to evaluate *before* that happens. The current LLGs support this. 

There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

branch_006.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Communicate Proposal Outcomes Clearly' is too narrow and focuses on a specific sub-task (communication/feedback) rather than the complete functional intention of the Administration Department regarding supplier proposals. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Proposal Evaluation and Response' accurately captures the full workflow described in the project description: evaluating proposals (reviewing details, pricing, etc.), making a decision (accept, reject, revise), providing feedback, and communicating the outcome. The existing HLG 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' covers the evaluation/decision aspect, but the original HLG's focus on communication is distinct yet incomplete on its own. However, looking at the actor's description ('Evaluates product proposals, requests revisions, and receives reminders') and the project text, the core responsibility is the end-to-end management of the proposal lifecycle from the admin side. The original HLG is a fragment of this larger goal. The reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Proposal Evaluation and Response' is a better, more comprehensive representation of the actor's intention. Since 'Efficiently Evaluate Product Proposals' already exists, one might argue for overlap, but 'Evaluate' usually implies the decision-making process, while 'Communicate' implies the output. The reconstruction combines these into a single coherent goal 'Manage... Evaluation and Response'. Given the instruction to rewrite if the original is 'narrow' or 'incorrectly scoped', and the reconstruction provides a more faithful and complete scope of the admin's role in this specific process (which includes both the evaluation logic and the response/communication logic), rewriting is appropriate to capture the full intent. Alternatively, one could argue that 'Efficiently Evaluate' covers the decision and 'Communicate' covers the output, but the project description treats this as a single continuous process: 'evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes... If revisions are requested... must explain them... supplier is notified'. The reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Proposal Evaluation and Response' is the most accurate high-level goal. The original is too narrow (only communication). Therefore, it should be rewritten to reflect the broader management of the evaluation and response cycle.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location.

During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.

The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products.

In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.

Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks.

Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application.

The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated.

When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.

The project description only explicitly supports the act of reporting (adding a comment) and the consequence (product not admitted). It does not explicitly describe a complex lifecycle of 'managing' reports (e.g., editing, submitting, monitoring status) for the Goods-Receiving Staff. The staff's role is primarily to verify and report. The existing HLG 'Accurately Verify Delivered Goods' covers the verification aspect. The act of reporting is a distinct functional intention from verification. The original name 'Report Product Discrepancies' is accurate and reasonably scoped to the action described in the text. The reconstruction 'Manage...' might be slightly over-scoped if it implies a full CRUD lifecycle not detailed in the text for this specific actor. However, 'Report' is a specific action. Is it too narrow? The text says 'reports it by adding a comment'. This is a single action. The reconstruction implies a process. Given the instruction to keep supported and reasonably scoped intentions, and that 'Report' is the specific action taken, it is a valid HLG. However, looking at the other HLGs, 'Accurately Verify Delivered Goods' and 'Optimize Product Placement' are the other two main tasks. 'Report Product Discrepancies' fits well as the third. The reconstruction 'Manage Product Discrepancy Reports' is arguably less faithful to the simple 'report by adding a comment' description than 'Report Product Discrepancies'. Therefore, the original is kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the actions required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Report Product Discrepancies'. The documentation states that if a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted. The LLGs cover: identifying the item (llg_001), creating the report (llg_002), adding the required comment (llg_003), uploading evidence (llg_004, which is a reasonable extension for 'documenting' problems, though not explicitly mandated, it supports the goal), submitting the report (llg_005), and viewing/monitoring reports (llg_006). The action of 'not admitting the product' is a state change or consequence of the report submission/verification process, often handled by the system or the verification HLG ('Accurately Verify Delivered Goods'). The HLG 'Report Product Discrepancies' focuses on the documentation and reporting aspect. The existing LLGs capture the creation, detailing, submission, and retrieval of these reports. There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by this specific HLG that are absent from the LLGs. The sibling HLG 'Accurately Verify Delivered Goods' likely covers the initial check and the decision to reject/admit, while this HLG covers the reporting mechanism. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers. Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it until a response is received. The administration department is notified whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order information. If revisions are requested, the administration department must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity, and store location.

During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.

The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products.

In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier, who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.

Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue, select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer through supported banks.

Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated application.

The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets. Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent. The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service statistics are updated.

When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket is automatically considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.
